Marissa / Team —

Draft procurement sequencing below (high-level milestones and owners). I left notes where legal review typically adds time.

Milestone A — MSA redline capture (3/16–3/20)
- Owner: BrightLeaf legal (primary), Redwood legal (response)
- Deliverable: tracked redline doc + issue log
- Risk: complex IP/data language could add +3 business days if custom clauses required

Milestone B — DPA & security addendum (3/18–3/22)
- Owner: BrightLeaf security & Redwood privacy/security
- Deliverable: final DPA with KMS integration appendix if required
- Note: if customer needs HSM-backed KMS or local on-prem key store, add 2–3 weeks ops work (flag early)

Milestone C — Pilot acceptance (3/22–4/2)
- Owner: BrightLeaf engineering (test lead), Redwood CS (runbook)
- Deliverable: acceptance report (latency/throughput, data retention verification, sample audit logs)
- Acceptance criteria (short list): sustained 95th percentile latency < 200ms for target prompt mix; KV cache behavior matches baseline; audit log export validated

Milestone D — Order form finalization & signature (4/5 target)
- Owner: Procurement leads
- Deliverable: signed order form (capacity, billing term, start date)
- Note: if order includes Dedicated reserved capacity we need PO lead time of 2–3 weeks after signature for capacity allocation

If we want to hit the first-half-of-April window, we should compress the MSA/DPA overlap and pre-schedule legal working sessions. I'll draft a short redline playbook (common clauses + preferred language) to speed signoff.

—Jordan

Team / Evan —

Thanks — quick ops checklist and timeline notes from infra/engr perspective:

1) KMS: If BrightLeaf wants customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS/HSM) we'll need their key provisioning details and IAM mapping. Typical lead time: 5–7 business days once keys are provisioned by the customer. If they require on-prem HSM, add 2–3 weeks and a private deployment plan.

2) Network: VPC peering or private link setup (for private deployment) — 3–5 business days after networking approvals and firewall rules.

3) Pilot plan (two-week run):
- Week A (3/22–3/28): soak + synthetic load verification (CS runs scripts, we provide runbook)
- Week B (3/29–4/2): targeted customer prompts + audit log verification

4) Acceptance artifacts we'll provide: runbook, perf report (p50/p95/p99), sample audit logs, token accounting export, and basic cost estimate for observed throughput.

5) Dedicated capacity note: If they want reserved GPUs, procurement needs to sign order form with a minimum 30-day lead for capacity allocation and quantized SKU selection.

I'll attach a short evaluation checklist and a template test plan to the MAP file tonight. If legal needs specific language about key custody we should add that to the DPA appendix now.

—Aditya
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
